classification.difficultyReason: Compare an area upper bound with achievable rectangular packings; the second area bound cannot be attained.

content.prompt: Cartons are stored in a large room. In order to allow access to the boxes, the available space in the room is a $7\text{ m}$ by $7\text{ m}$ square. Cartons cannot be stacked on top of each other.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Some cartons have a base $3\text{ m}$ by $2\text{ m}$. By comparing areas, what is the maximum number of these cartons that can be stored in this room?

answer.worked:
The available area is $49\text{ m}^2$ and each carton occupies $6\text{ m}^2$.

$$\begin{align*}6n&\le49\\n&\le\frac{49}{6}\end{align*}$$

Since $n$ is a whole number, the area bound is 8 cartons.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Draw a diagram to show how this can be achieved.

answer.worked: Arrange two cartons along each side in a pinwheel pattern. The eight $3\text{ m}\times2\text{ m}$ rectangles leave a $1\text{ m}\times1\text{ m}$ central gap.

spec.description: Eight unshaded rectangles in a pinwheel packing, with a central unit-square gap; dimensions follow the teacher solution.
spec.mathematics: Eight 3 by 2 rectangles fit without overlap in a 7 by 7 square.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Other cartons have a base $4\text{ m}$ by $2\text{ m}$. By comparing areas, what is the maximum number of these cartons that can be stored in this room?

answer.worked:
Each carton occupies $8\text{ m}^2$.

$$\begin{align*}8n&\le49\\n&\le\frac{49}{8}\end{align*}$$

Since $n$ is a whole number, comparing areas gives an upper bound of 6 cartons.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: It is not possible to store the number of boxes found in part i. What is the actual maximum number of these boxes that can be stored in this room?

answer.worked: The area calculation does not ensure that the rectangles fit. Three cartons can stand side by side across a $6\text{ m}\times4\text{ m}$ region, with one rotated carton above them. This gives the maximum of 4 cartons.

spec.description: Three upright rectangles beneath one horizontal rectangle, reconstructed from the teacher solution without decorative shading.
spec.mathematics: Four 4 by 2 rectangles fit without overlap in a 7 by 7 square.
